title: Looking back: the depths
hookLine: themes, Bhagats, rehat, history and grief carried carefully

lines: A HUNDRED DAYS OF DEEP WATER.
cards: There's a point, swimming out from a beach, where your feet reach down and find nothing. The water gets darker and colder. Then, with a steady breath, something changes.
The water holds you up. The shore behind you looks small. Camp five was that kind of water.
A hundred days past where the feet can touch: the Granth's biggest ideas, the Bhagats, the Sikh way of life, centuries of history, and a week of real grief.

teach.b: It began with the shape of the Guru Granth Sahib: fourteen hundred thirty pages, each called an ang, a limb; many voices, one Guru.
Then the great themes: hukam, the order; haumai, the ego that is its own disease and holds its own cure; naam, the Name; nadar, the kindly glance of grace.

The five thieves in the house of the mind, and the five virtues that guard it. The Guru asking why woman should be called lesser, when kings are born of her. Asking about the light in a person, not their caste.
Then the Bhagats: Kabir the weaver and Farid the Sufi, whose hymns the Gurus kept beside their own.
Then rehat, the Sikh way of life: kesh, kangha, kara, kachhera and kirpan, amrit, the written code, the many ways of being Sikh, the saint-soldier.

Then the long history: Banda Singh, the years in the forests, the two ghallugharas, Ranjit Singh covering the Harmandir Sahib in gold, annexation, Jallianwala Bagh, the peaceful struggle for the gurdwaras, Partition, and a door opening at Kartarpur.
Then 1984, carried as carefully as this path could. And the diaspora, strangers who became neighbors everywhere.
The Guru Granth Sahib often pictures the world as a vast, frightening ocean, the bhavjal, and the Guru's word as the boat that carries you across. That's a fair picture of camp five.
Some of it was beautiful and wide open.
Some of it was dark and cold and hard to look at. Nobody had to understand all of it to get across. The way over was a day at a time, with the Guru's word as the boat.

how: Sikhs deepen their understanding through katha (explanation of the hymns), study of the Guru Granth Sahib and Sikh history, and remembrance of the panth's struggles in the daily Ardas.

o: a dive into one hymn, read word by word
a look back at the year's deepest lessons
a week spent only on Sikh history dates

p: a page of the Granth: a limb
the world pictured as an ocean

s: the Guru Granth Sahib holds only the Gurus' hymns
it keeps the hymns of Bhagats like Kabir and Farid beside the Gurus' own.
the Granth often pictures the Guru's word as a boat across a frightening ocean
the world is the bhavjal; the word carries you across.
the Granth calls haumai, ego, a disease with no cure
it calls ego a long disease that holds its own cure.

games.q: in the Granth's picture, you're facing a vast, frightening ocean. what carries you across?
o: your own strength as a swimmer.
the Guru's word, like a boat.
waiting on the shore until it's calm.
games.why: the hymns picture the world as the bhavjal and the Guru's word as the boat that carries you over.

practice: Let one hard part of this year's path come back to you: a teaching that challenged you, a story that hurt to hear, a question you still can't answer.
Don't try to fix it or solve it; let it sit beside you like a companion on a long swim, and notice that you're still here, still breathing, held up. Then let it rest.

wordCard.voice: Looking back. Camp five, the depths: the Granth's themes, the Bhagats, rehat, history, and grief carried carefully.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: bhavjal, the world-ocean; in the hymns, the Guru's word is the boat across it.

carryVoice: Your line: deep water, crossed. This year, you've already crossed it, one day at a time. See you tomorrow.
